lines.text: {settlement} is here because the roads are here; the town is what grew in the place where stopping made sense.
Nobody chose {settlement}'s site. The geography chose it, and the town has been agreeing with the geography ever since.
{settlement} sits where the roads meet and eats what the roads bring: the ground under the town was never the reason for the town.
A crossing feeds a town before its fields do, and {settlement} has never had it the other way round.

keyGuarantees: config.tradeRouteAccess port (any terrain: riverside ports fold here too, so coast is NOT guaranteed)

lines.text: {settlement} exists because of the water, and nothing about the town makes sense without it.
{settlement}'s living comes off the quay; the fields behind it are a convenience the town could manage without.
What {settlement} eats arrives by the same water that gives the town its trade, which makes the harbour the whole of the argument for the place.
{settlement} looks seaward for everything, including dinner.
{settlement} is built on its water because the water is the cheapest thing here to move goods on.
Every decision {settlement} has ever made about where to put a building started with the river.
{settlement}'s ground gives less than the town needs and the river makes up the rest, which is why the town is on the river and not on better ground.
A river town can be short of fields and long of custom, and {settlement} is both.
{settlement} is out of reach of the trade roads, and self-sufficiency here is a constraint rather than an aspiration.
{settlement} produces what {settlement} uses, because the alternative is a long journey for it.

{settlement} is out of reach of the trade roads and cannot fully feed itself; what the land does not give arrives dearly (by sanctioned caravan, by seasonal access, by patronage, by ration), or it does not arrive.
The gap between what {settlement} grows and what {settlement} eats is closed at a price, and the price is visible in the market before anyone explains it.

keyGuarantees: config.tradeRouteAccess road, mountain_pass, mountain_road, desert_road, or absent (originRoutePoolKey fallback)

lines.text: {settlement} is on a road and lives off the road: goods in, goods out, people through.
{settlement} is here because somebody, once, found this a reasonable distance from the last place.
What {settlement} cannot grow, the road brings, and the road is therefore not a convenience for this town but a condition of it.
{settlement} is a road town that has outgrown its fields, and it is buying the difference.

lines.text: {settlement} no longer serves an economic function for its region. It is the economic function.
A place this size stops being a settlement in the country and becomes the thing the country is arranged around.
Nobody in {settlement} thinks of the region as somewhere else.

pools.ruling: Not scoped: size prose; food claims ride the deficit mark.

lines.text: {settlement} produces what it consumes and consumes what it produces; trade widens the margin rather than supplying it.
{settlement} is large enough that its appetites outrun its fields: what the city eats, the city cannot fully grow.
{settlement} is big enough to have quarters that do not know each other.

pools.ruling: Not scoped; colour: size prose the key owns.

lines.text: {settlement} is small enough that every household knows its purpose, and surplus, where there is any, is modest.
{settlement} is a handful of roofs with a reason, and the reason is usually the ground.
{settlement}'s whole economy fits on one page and always has room left.

lines.text: {settlement} is the size that a place of this kind settles at, and it has settled there.
{settlement} is neither small enough to be simple nor large enough to be complicated, and it manages both ways.
{settlement} is a town, in the ordinary sense, and the ordinariness is accurate.
